name: Default incubator rubric (editable; replace with the program's real criteria)

criteria.name: Problem & customer pain
criteria.description: Is there a specific, real problem for an identifiable group of people?

anchors.1: No clear problem, or a generic statement with no affected group.
anchors.3: A real problem is named and a group is implied, but evidence of the pain is thin.
anchors.5: A specific problem, a clearly defined group, and concrete evidence of the pain (interviews, numbers, observations).

criteria.name: Solution & differentiation
criteria.description: Does the solution fit the problem, and is it meaningfully different from what exists?

anchors.1: Solution is vague, unrelated to the problem, or buzzwords only.
anchors.3: Solution fits the problem but looks similar to existing options.
anchors.5: Clear solution with a specific reason it beats existing alternatives.

criteria.name: Market & target customers
criteria.description: Who pays, how many are there, and can they be reached?

anchors.3: Target customers named, with a rough sense of size or reach.
anchors.5: Specific paying segment, a reasoned size estimate, and a believable way to reach them.

criteria.name: Traction & validation
criteria.description: Evidence that real people want this: pilots, users, revenue, letters of intent, interviews.

anchors.1: No evidence beyond the founders' belief.
anchors.3: Some validation: interviews, a prototype tested with a few users, or waitlist.
anchors.5: Paying customers, signed pilots, or strong repeat usage, with numbers.

criteria.name: Business model
criteria.description: A believable way to earn money that matches who the customer is.

anchors.1: No revenue model, or 'we will figure it out'.
anchors.3: A revenue model is stated but pricing or unit economics are not reasoned.
anchors.5: Clear who pays, how much, and why the numbers can work.

criteria.name: Team & founder-market fit
criteria.description: Does the team have the skills and context to execute this specific idea?

anchors.1: No information about the team, or no relevant skills.
anchors.3: Relevant skills for part of the work; gaps not addressed.
anchors.5: Complementary skills, direct experience of the problem, and a track record of shipping.

criteria.name: Feasibility & execution plan
criteria.description: Can this be built and launched with the resources and time they describe?

anchors.1: No plan, or the plan is clearly unrealistic.
anchors.3: A plausible plan with some unrealistic or missing steps.
anchors.5: Concrete milestones, realistic scope, and the ask matches what the program can give.
